metadata.title: llama-annotation-pipeline: Snakemake workflow and documented commands for homology-based and ab initio annotation of the Lama glama genome
metadata.description:
Reproducible Snakemake workflow for the structural annotation of a chromosome-level Lama glama genome assembly by homology transfer and ab initio prediction, with evaluation against an external reference.

The workflow generates four proteome sets and a combined candidate reference proteome of 20,708 sequences, stratified into three nested confidence layers: 18,920 high-confidence models with an intact reading frame and detectable homology in an external reference, 1,313 extended-reference models failing one or both criteria, and 475 candidates from the ab initio prediction.

The Snakemake workflow covers Liftoff, miniprot, proteome extraction and BUSCO. LiftOn, Helixer, InterProScan and DIAMOND were run manually, with the commands documented in REPRODUCIBILITY.md.

No sequence or annotation data are tracked in this repository. The annotation sets and proteomes are deposited separately under CC0-1.0, concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21445839.

metadata.title: httk Extension Package for Brain and Adipose Compartments
metadata.description: The included software package provides an extension to the high-throughput toxicokinetics (httk) R package (v2.2.2). While the standard httk framework offers generalized pbtk modeling, this modification integrates specific compartments for adipose and brain tissues, following modeling framework described by Davidson-Fritz et al. (2025). The model utilizes a system of ordinary differential equations (ODEs) implemented through C script for computational efficiency. Key features include updated chemical-specific parameterization and the new “solve_pbtk_adipose_complexbrain” function, allowing for predictions of chemical distribution in these compartments.

metadata.title: Aircraft Simulation Core 2.0.0
metadata.description: This software is built using this mathematical model which derives the kinematics, dynamics, and control for a point-mass aircraft operating in a wind field and moving across a surface. The mathematical model is a system of equations that connects the state variables of true airspeed, flight path angle, and heading angle. Then, coordinate frame transformations are used to derive 3-dimensional motion on a plane and an ellipsoid, providing propagation of altitude and position.

Dependencies, execution instructions, and structural data formatting details are provided in the primary README file contained within the repository archive.

metadata.title: Ultralytics YOLO
metadata.description:
🌟 Summary

🚀 Ultralytics v8.4.132 improves dataset efficiency, hardware compatibility, export workflows, and experiment-tracking documentation, with the headline feature being finer control over test-split downloads.

📊 Key Changes

  • 🎯 Test-split control with fraction (PR #25966 — @fcakyon)

    • List-based fraction now supports train, validation, and test splits.
    • Use a third value to limit test data or set it to 0 to skip test-image downloads entirely.
    • Existing two-value lists remain compatible and continue using the full test split.
    • The same split-selection behavior is shared across training, validation, dataset conversion, and export calibration.

  • ⚡ More efficient NDJSON workflows

    • Platform NDJSON runs no longer need to download unused test images, which can significantly reduce transfer time, storage use, and bandwidth during multi-dataset sweeps.

  • 🩹 Corrected NMS and validation on Ascend NPU

    • NMS now uses the optimized torchvision path on supported Ascend NPU setups while continuing to avoid unsupported XPU behavior.
    • Fixes repeated NMS time-limit warnings and prevents incomplete batches from producing incorrect mAP results.

  • 📚 Improved YOLO26 end-to-end and export guidance

    • Documentation now more accurately describes NMS-free detection, segmentation, pose, and OBB models.
    • Clarifies export-format fallbacks, quantization limitations, Hailo behavior, detection limits, and expected accuracy trade-offs.
    • Updates performance claims and explains when custom post-processing or NMS is still required.

  • 🔄 Broader support for exported non-YOLO models

    • Documents loading generic exported models through YOLO() when task and imgsz are supplied explicitly.
    • Adds guidance for using format-specific backend classes and explains input-layout, autograd, and post-processing differences.
    • Corrects TensorFlow SavedModel, LiteRT, and numerical-parity documentation.

  • 🧪 Better classification subset sampling

    • Fraction-based sampling for local classification datasets now selects images across classes instead of taking a class-ordered prefix.
    • Produces more representative subsets for quick experiments and validation.

  • 📈 Updated experiment-tracking integrations

    • Ray Tune now uses its public context and reporting APIs.
    • ClearML, Comet, TensorBoard, MLflow, Ray Tune, and W&B instructions now better match current callback behavior.
    • Neptune integration and settings were retired following the service shutdown.
    • MLflow environment-variable handling is more flexible, and TensorBoard setup is clearly documented as optional.

  • 🧩 Additional training and export corrections

    • RT-DETR documentation recommends disabling deterministic mode on CUDA, since its attention operation cannot provide fully deterministic backward training.
    • Copy-Paste augmentation is correctly documented for both segment and OBB tasks.
    • Classification color-jitter settings are clarified when automatic augmentation is disabled.
    • IMX exports no longer reject end-to-end models at the exporter entry point.
    • CLA workflow matching now accepts signature comments with surrounding whitespace or text.

🎯 Purpose & Impact

  • 💾 Lower data-transfer costs: Users running Platform or NDJSON workflows can avoid downloading test data they do not need.
  • ⏱️ Faster experimentation: Smaller, representative dataset subsets make tuning and iteration quicker without changing existing two-item fraction usage.
  • 📊 More trustworthy metrics: Ascend NPU validation now processes complete batches, improving the reliability of reported mAP.
  • 🚀 Easier deployment: Clearer YOLO26 export guidance helps users understand when NMS-free inference works and when a traditional NMS pipeline is necessary.
  • 🌍 Better hardware coverage: NPU and export-path fixes improve compatibility across specialized accelerators and deployment formats.
  • 🧭 Smoother integrations: Updated tracking documentation reduces setup confusion, while users migrating from Neptune should select an active integration such as ClearML, Comet, MLflow, TensorBoard, W&B, or the Ultralytics Platform.

What's Changed

  • Match CLA signature comments by substring in the workflow gate by @glenn-jocher in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/25970
  • Fix NMS time-limit truncation and wrong mAP on Ascend NPU by @idwenhui in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/25963
  • Update experiment tracking callbacks and docs by @glenn-jocher in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/25972
  • Add https://youtu.be/rMllxg8ZLs8 to docs by @RizwanMunawar in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/25975
  • Document running non-YOLO exports through Ultralytics and correct parity claims by @raimbekovm in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/25974
  • Correct end-to-end detection guide claims and export fallback coverage by @raimbekovm in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/25971
  • Correct copy-paste task attribution and the export conf default claim by @raimbekovm in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/25969
  • Fix classification fraction sampling by @JESUSROYETH in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/25968
  • Recommend deterministic=False for RT-DETR training by @artest08 in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/25965
  • Extend fraction to the test split by @fcakyon in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/25966

New Contributors

metadata.title: Computational Files for "Gibbs Phenomenon for a Modified Fourier Series"
metadata.description:
This record contains computational files associated with the article “Gibbs Phenomenon for a Modified Fourier Series.” The files include executable Maple worksheets used to perform the modified Fourier series computations, a representative saved Maple output file, and an Excel workbook summarizing results from the final computational runs.

The Maple worksheets were created using Maple 2023 and require Maple software to open and execute. Information about Maple is available from Maplesoft: https://www.maplesoft.com/products/maple/.

Files included:

MFS-OptionsCoded-2026-Final.mw — Main Maple 2023 executable worksheet implementing the modified Fourier series computations using the classical Gram–Schmidt (CGS) method. User-selectable options include numerical or analytical integration, orthogonal or orthonormal bases, and alternative methods for locating the overshoot.

ReadSavedMapleData.mw — Maple 2023 executable worksheet that reads a saved output file generated by MFS-OptionsCoded-2026-Final.mw, extracts the stored function, basis, overshoot data, and partial sums, and uses them to recreate figures and plots used in the associated paper.

MFSw(sinx)2_n1_100.m — Representative saved Maple output file generated by MFS-OptionsCoded-2026-Final.mw for the weight function w(x) = sin^2(x) and n = 1,...,100. The file stores Maple objects including the function being approximated and its odd extension, the computed basis functions, partial sums, and numerical overshoot results. It can be read and used with ReadSavedMapleData.mw.

SummaryofFinalRuns_n30.xlsx — Excel workbook summarizing the final Maple-generated results for n = 30 and powers r = 0,...,4 for the weight functions w(x) = sin^r(x) and w(x) = x^r. The reported quantities include the size of the overshoot, change in overshoot, and location of the overshoot.
keywords: Gibbs Phenomenon, Fourier Series, Orthogonality and Weight Functions

metadata.title: Epistemic Observability in Language Models: PACMI 2026 reproduction artifact
metadata.description:
Corrects the self-report confidence data reported in ai-honesty issue #1 by Chris Brew.

The original extractor decoded the prompt along with the generation and took the first integer found — usually the 0 in the prompt's own "scale of 0-100" text. The corruption was asymmetric (47.2% of knowable vs 31.2% of unknowable rows zeroed), which manufactured an apparent "self-report inversion".

Changes

  • data/exp27_bounded_verification_20260206_205725.csv — corrected values in self_report_confidence; the original values preserved as self_report_confidence_broken so the change is auditable.
  • Figure 2 regenerated from the corrected column.
  • REPRODUCTION.md documents the correction and its provenance.

Corrected reading: self-report is compressed near the ceiling (knowable 0.975, unknowable 0.733, AUC 0.66–0.92 per family) rather than inverted. The impossibility argument does not depend on inversion.

Unaffected: Figure 3 (budget curve) and the Exp34 pipeline table — neither reads the self-report column. All twelve budget-curve values and the Exp34 numbers reproduce exactly.

metadata.title: vertesy/Stringendo
metadata.description:
Stringendo 1.2.5 — Improvements and Maintenance

A small, focused release: hardening of the string/path utility functions plus new CI.

Bug fixes

  • Hardened path and separator helpers against false positives and runtime errors; fixed the percentage formatter and numeric checker to correctly handle NA/NaN inputs.
  • Fixed brittle, incorrect regex-based cleanup in PasteDirNameFromFlags() and PasteOutdirFromFlags() that could mangle directory names — e.g. stripping meaningful leading dots or breaking the trailing-slash convention. Both now reuse the package's own canonical helpers (ReplaceRepeatedDots(), RemoveTrailingDots(), FixPath()) instead of ad-hoc regexes.
  • toDotSeparated() now returns its result invisibly (consistent with similar functions) and no longer errors if the optional clipr package isn't installed.

Infrastructure

  • Added a GitHub Actions R CMD check workflow, so every push/PR to main and dev is automatically checked for package integrity.

Validation & docs

  • Added input checks (stopifnot) and usage examples to the fixed flag/path functions, with documentation regenerated to match.

No breaking changes.

Full Changelog: https://github.com/vertesy/Stringendo/compare/v1.1.0...v1.2.5

metadata.title: vertesy/Seurat.utils
metadata.description:
Seurat.utils 2.9.10 — Improvements and Maintenance

Roughly a year of incremental fixes (v2.9.0 → v2.9.10). No major new features, but a solid batch of real bug fixes plus general hardening.

Bug fixes

  • addTranslatedMetadata() was ignoring the suffix argument and a logical flag — now respected.
  • getMetaColnames(), getMetadataColumn(), and getCellIDs.from.meta() had bugs with empty matches, a stray numeric offset, and NA/NaN handling — all fixed.
  • Combined metadata extraction no longer collapses to a plain vector when a column is removed — stays a proper data frame.
  • add.meta.tags() was silently using a global variable instead of the tags list you actually passed in.
  • processSeuratObject() no longer errors when variables.2.regress is NULL.
  • Calc.Cor.Seurat() used a raw cell count instead of actual cell names when skipping downsampling — fixed.
  • Removed a leftover browser() debugger breakpoint in RenameGenesSeurat() that would have frozen any script calling it.
  • RemoveGenesSeurat() rewritten for Seurat v5's layered RNA assay, replacing fragile version-specific slot manipulation.
  • Cleaned up a few files that had unresolved git merge-conflict markers accidentally committed into source and docs.

Changed behavior

  • Serialization migrated from the now-archived qs package to its successor, qs2 (affects .qs file save/load calls).
  • Convert10Xfolders() gained a save parameter to control .qs output; the older Convert10Xfolders.old is now formally deprecated in its favor.

Hardening

  • Added input validation (type/range/presence checks) across many functions — PlotUpdateStats, Calc.Cor.Seurat, Convert10Xfolders, metadata and PCA/UMAP helpers — so bad inputs now fail fast with a clear message instead of a confusing downstream error.

Docs & cleanup

  • Documented the package's coding style (native pipe |>, tidyverse conventions), simplified overly verbose Roxygen descriptions, and fixed broken documentation examples and a broken README install command.
  • Fixed numerous typos across comments and docs, and clarified a couple of confusingly-named internal variables.

No breaking changes for normal usage — the one thing to note is the qs → qs2 serialization swap; re-save any long-term .qs files with the new package if you depend on them.

Full Changelog: https://github.com/vertesy/Seurat.utils/compare/v2.9.0...v2.9.10

metadata.description:
Chembience is a containerized platform for building chemical-informatics applications with RDKit and RDKit-enabled PostgreSQL. It can generate ready-to-customize Django, FastAPI, JupyterLab, or RDKit projects with development and production deployment tooling included. Each generated project is designed to become an independent application, with Docker Compose and Kubernetes deployment options.

This repository supersedes the original Chembience implementation (versions 0.4.0 and earlier) and includes versions later than 0.5.0
